## Circular to Intermediaries

## Marketing of Hedge Funds

The  Securities  and  Futures  Commission  notes  that  a  wide  range  of  collective  investment schemes  is  being  sold  in  the  retail  market.  Most  recently,  the  Commission  has  authorized public hedge funds. As a matter of principle, the Commission welcomes product innovation and the expansion of investment choices for investors. However, in view of the diversity and complexity of hedge funds and the inherent risks involved, the Commission wishes to remind intermediaries that they should comply with the Code of Conduct for Persons Licensed by or Registered with the SFC ('Code of Conduct') and adopt fair dealing when marketing hedge funds to investors.

Hedge funds are a type of collective investment schemes. There is no universal definition of hedge funds.  They  vary  enormously  in  terms  of  their  investment  returns,  risk  profiles  and investment strategies. Although hedge funds are often marketed as 'all weather' funds that are able to perform under different market conditions, they are not 'sure-win' products. For some hedge funds, substantial loss of capital is possible. Investors should make sure that they fully understand the nature and risks involved before buying hedge funds.

Here are some key measures that intermediaries are expected to observe with regards to the marketing of hedge funds except where these are waived under the Code of Conduct:

1. Know  Your  Client: To  ensure that hedge funds are suitable for their clients, intermediaries  should  take  all  reasonable  steps  beforehand  to  obtain  and  verify  the identity of the client as well as to establish the financial situation, investment experience, investment  objectives,  time  horizon  and  risk  tolerance  of  the  client.  This  will  help intermediaries  to  properly  assess  their  client's  ability  to  bear  the  financial  risks  and potential losses that may arise from investing in hedge funds.
2. Give Reasonable Advice: Intermediaries should provide clear and reasonable advice to clients  and  ensure  any  representations  made  and  information  provided  to  the  client  are accurate and not misleading. When  recommending  hedge  funds  to  their clients, intermediaries should ensure that the suitability of the recommendation for those clients is reasonable in all the circumstances.

![Image](data:image/png;base64,)

3. Fit and Proper Staff: The senior management of intermediaries should ensure that the persons  they  employ  or  appoint  to  conduct  business  are  suitably  qualified  and  have received proper training to a level commensurate with their responsibilities in marketing hedge funds.
4. Information  for  Clients: Intermediaries  should  provide  their  clients  with  pertinent information  regarding  the  hedge  funds.    These  include  the  provision  of  the  scheme prospectus  prior  to  subscription  by  the  client,  and  where  appropriate,  other  relevant scheme  information  that  would  assist  the  client  in  making  an  informed  investment decision.

The Commission strongly urges intermediaries to provide clients with relevant, balanced and responsible investor education materials in marketing hedge funds. The Commission has issued education leaflets titled "How Much Do You Know About Hedge Funds" and "Ten Questions to Ask Before Investing in a Fund". Copies of the leaflets are available by calling  Investor  Education  and  Communications  Department  at  2842-7711.    Other investor education information on hedge funds and traditional funds is available on the SFC-operated Electronic Investor Resources Centre at www.hkeirc.org .

5. Internal  Control  Procedures :  Intermediaries  should  set  appropriate  internal  controls procedures  with  respect  to  the  marketing  of  hedge  funds.  Their  senior  management assumes full responsibility for the development, implementation and on-going effectiveness of the internal controls and the adherence thereto.

For more details, intermediaries should refer to the Code of Conduct which is available on the Commission's website at www.hksfc.org.hk .
